I am working on Bergman's Diamond Lemma (toward the PBW theorem). It is convenient to have monomial orders for non-commutative monomials, in particular, a non-commutative analog of DegLex. Is there a code for such orders?

Commutative monomials are implemented as elements of σ →₀ ℕ representing exponents of the monomials. Non-commutative monomials are implemented (in FreeMonoid α) as elements of List α representing the monomials themselves.

As a new user of Lean, I tried to introduce another LinearOrder on List α respecting (degree of monomial = length of list). Now I am not sure that the idea was good.
Perhaps I'm wrong, but there is something I don't understand: a LinearOrder is antisymmetric, so if M ≤ L and L ≤ M then M = L: but if M, L have the same length they need not coincide.

Filippo A. E. Nuccio said:

Perhaps I'm wrong, but there is something I don't understand: a LinearOrder is antisymmetric, so if M ≤ L and L ≤ M then M = L: but if M, L have the same length they need not coincide.

Sorry, I was too brief in my explanation. The elements of a non-commutative FreeMonoid α and elements of List α can be considered as words built from the elements of α as letters. If we have a LinearOrder α, that is a linear order on letters, there are many ways to extend it to orders on words.

In Lean, the List α is lexicographical ordered (Lex order). I need another order on words (so-called DegLex order) with two-step ordering:
(1) shorter words standing before longer words and
(2) the words with the same length (degree) ordered lexicographically.
(The second step of the ordering was implicit in my previous message and may give the answer to your question).
A code demonstrating that LinearOrder α induces Lex order on List α :

import Mathlib

variable {α : Type*} [LinearOrder α]
example (a b : α) (hab : a < b) :
    [a, b] < [b, a] := by
  simp [@List.cons_lt_cons_iff]
  tauto
-- an example when a longer word is smaller in `Lex` order: `ab < b`
example (a b : α) (hab : a < b) :
    [a, b] < [b] := by
  simpa [@List.cons_lt_cons_iff]

DegLex order is already implemented for commutative monomials in Mathlib.Data.Finsupp.MonomialOrder.DegLex
I am interested in its non-commutative analog.
The file you link to defines docs#Finsupp.DegLex . Looks like you want to define List.DegLex or FreeMonoid.DegLex?

Kevin Buzzard said:

Looks like you want to define List.DegLex or FreeMonoid.DegLex?

I borrowed a pattern from Finsupp.DegLex to define FreeMonoid.DegLex. It looks working.
I have a problem with using < notation and a problem with coercion from the List to FreeMonoid.

import Mathlib

variable {α : Type*} [LinearOrder α]

open FreeMonoid

instance : LT α := inferInstance

variable (a b : α)
variable [LT (FreeMonoid α)]

instance : Coe α (FreeMonoid α) := ⟨FreeMonoid.of⟩
instance : Coe (List α) (FreeMonoid α) := ⟨FreeMonoid.ofList⟩

/- Coercion from the List to FreeMonoid on RHS of the first example is not working? -/
example :  (a : FreeMonoid α) * b = ([a, b] : FreeMonoid α) := by rfl
example :  (a : FreeMonoid α) * b = (FreeMonoid.ofList [a, b]) := by rfl

/-- DegLex order for FreeMonoid α -/
/- The pattern is borrowed from the original DegLex file:
DegLex order is a Lex Product order on length of List (degree) and then on List
-/
def FreeMonoid.DegLex : (FreeMonoid α) → (FreeMonoid α) → Prop :=
  Function.onFun (Prod.Lex (. < .) (. < .)) (fun x ↦ (x.length, x.toList))

variable (hab : a < b)

-- Ordered by degree
-- `b < a * b`
example : DegLex (b : FreeMonoid α)  (a * b) := by
  simp [FreeMonoid.DegLex, Function.onFun, Prod.lex_def]

-- For the same degree, the order is Lex
-- `a < b`
example : DegLex (a : FreeMonoid α) b := by
  simpa [FreeMonoid.DegLex, Function.onFun, Prod.lex_def, List.cons_lt_cons_iff]

-- For the same degree, the order is Lex
-- `a * a < a * b`
example: DegLex ((a : FreeMonoid α) * (a : FreeMonoid α))
    (a  * (b : FreeMonoid α)) := by
  simpa [FreeMonoid.DegLex, Function.onFun, Prod.lex_def, List.cons_lt_cons_iff]

instance : LT (FreeMonoid α) := ⟨ FreeMonoid.DegLex ⟩
/- I can not prove `a < b` with LT while all is OK with DegLex in the above second example -/
example  : (a : FreeMonoid α) < b := by
  sorry
  simp [FreeMonoid.DegLex, Function.onFun, Prod.lex_def, List.cons_lt_cons_iff]

instance : LT α := inferInstance

That's unnecessary -- inferInstance means "check it's there already", and it is because alpha is a linear order. But more to the point

variable [LT (FreeMonoid α)]

that is positively dangerous! It means "put a random < on FreeMonoid α, totally unrelated to the order on α."

Everything seems to be working fine with only minor adjustments:

import Mathlib

variable {α : Type*} [LinearOrder α]

open FreeMonoid

variable (a b : α)

instance : Coe α (FreeMonoid α) := ⟨FreeMonoid.of⟩
instance : Coe (List α) (FreeMonoid α) := ⟨FreeMonoid.ofList⟩

/- Coercion from the List to FreeMonoid works fine -/
example :  (a : FreeMonoid α) * b = [a, b] := by rfl

/-- DegLex order for FreeMonoid α -/
/- The pattern is borrowed from the original DegLex file:
DegLex order is a Lex Product order on length of List (degree) and then on List
-/
def FreeMonoid.DegLex : (FreeMonoid α) → (FreeMonoid α) → Prop :=
  Function.onFun (Prod.Lex (. < .) (. < .)) (fun x ↦ (x.length, x.toList))

-- may as well define it now!
instance : LT (FreeMonoid α) := ⟨FreeMonoid.DegLex⟩

variable (hab : a < b)

-- make DegLex the "simp normal form", i.e. make the simplifier deconstruct `<`.
-- This might not be the best idea but it makes the proofs below work.
@[simp] lemma FreeMonoid.DegLex_def {x y : FreeMonoid α} : x < y ↔ FreeMonoid.DegLex x y :=
  Iff.rfl

-- Ordered by degree
-- `b < a * b`
example : (b : FreeMonoid α) < (a * b) := by
  simp [FreeMonoid.DegLex, Function.onFun, Prod.lex_def]

-- For the same degree, the order is Lex
-- `a < b`
example : (a : FreeMonoid α) < b := by
  simpa [FreeMonoid.DegLex, Function.onFun, Prod.lex_def, List.cons_lt_cons_iff]

-- For the same degree, the order is Lex
-- `a * a < a * b`
example: ((a : FreeMonoid α) * (a : FreeMonoid α)) < (a  * (b : FreeMonoid α)) := by
  simpa [FreeMonoid.DegLex, Function.onFun, Prod.lex_def, List.cons_lt_cons_iff]

/- Now works -/
example  : (a : FreeMonoid α) < b := by
  simpa [FreeMonoid.DegLex, Function.onFun, Prod.lex_def, List.cons_lt_cons_iff]

I think that ideally one would not let the simplifier unfold a < b and one should instead make simp lemmas about < on FreeMonoid whose proofs unfold the definition but whose statements do not. This would make for a nicer-looking theory.

Thank you very much!
I have one more (related?) question regarding coercion from the List to FreeMonoid on the last line of the following code. If I stand after by, I see that the list[a, b] is not transformed to a term of FreeMonoid. But rfl works. Is it OK? I thought that there is an idea not to mix an abstract FreeMonoid with its implementation by List. 

import Mathlib

variable {α : Type*} [LinearOrder α]

open FreeMonoid

variable (a b : α)

instance : Coe α (FreeMonoid α) := ⟨FreeMonoid.of⟩
instance : Coe (List α) (FreeMonoid α) := ⟨FreeMonoid.ofList⟩

/- Coercion from the List to FreeMonoid works fine -/
example :  (a : FreeMonoid α) * b = [a, b] := by rfl

Well I am very surprised by this!

As you can see, the goal you have constructed here is not type-correct.

I would have expected a small up-arrow. I think the reason for this is a bit technical and I am not 100% solid on this. Although I can never remember exactly how the up-arrow is triggered, for coercions I do remember that you are supposed to do two things (and I never really understood why): first register the Coe instance, and second tag the appropriate function with the @[coe] attribute. But you cannot tag the appropriate function with the attribute because FreeMonoid.ofList is an Equiv rather than a bare function.

In other parts of the library we have explicitly defined the bare function, used that as the coercion, and then tagged it with @[coe] and I think that this will get you the up-arrow. But then you'll have to make an API for this definition and it will be a bit of a bore.

Note that these comments do not apply to FreeMonoid.of, so you can do

attribute [coe] FreeMonoid.of

and get 

⊢ ↑a * ↑b = [a, b]

Huh, even that doesn't work!

import Mathlib

variable {α : Type*}

open FreeMonoid

variable (a b : α)

instance : Coe α (FreeMonoid α) := ⟨FreeMonoid.of⟩

def FreeMonoid.ofList_coe (x : List α) : FreeMonoid α := FreeMonoid.ofList x

instance : Coe (List α) (FreeMonoid α) := ⟨FreeMonoid.ofList_coe⟩

attribute [coe] FreeMonoid.of FreeMonoid.ofList_coe

/- Not type correct! -/
example :  (a : FreeMonoid α) * b = ↑[a, b] := by
  -- ⊢ ↑a * ↑b = [a, b]
  -- still doesn't work!
  rfl

I am very confused. Lean is seeing through the abstraction barrier and I can't make it do otherwise.
Lean will first check defeq before trying to synthesize a coercion
since defeq succeeds coercion is not tries
Gaargh but this is just the kind of abuse that v4.29 is trying to stamp out, right? It checks it at the wrong (too liberal) transparency maybe?
it checks at default transparency
And that's enough to see through the definition of FreeMonoid?
yes, since FreeMonoid is semireducible
see docs#Lean.ReducibilityStatus and docs#Lean.Meta.TransparencyMode

Is it an old code? ([] : FreeMonoid α) looks a bit strange.
Is attr := deprecated attributed to the main theorem or only to its additive version (as it was explained me by ChatGPT)? 

@[to_additive (attr := deprecated toList_one (since := "2026-03-26"))]
theorem toList_nil : toList ([] : FreeMonoid α) = [] := rfl

/FreeMonoid/Basic.lean#L117-L118
Trust the documentation over chatgpt: https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Algebra/FreeMonoid/Basic.html#FreeMonoid.toList_nil
Though that made me discover that the name of the new lemma is not additivized
So FreeAddMonoid.toList_nil claims the replacement is FreeMonoid.toList_one
